eli5.text: The team changed how the evaluation system sends email results by importing a needed function directly from the source code instead of relying on a pre-built package. The team, who run these automated tests and reviews, will no longer need to manually compile or build the integrations package before running the evaluations. This is behind-the-scenes maintenance to simplify the internal workflow and remove unnecessary setup steps.

ai.title: ftfilepickertopk003 added for top-2 file selection testing
ai.summary: New finetuned model `ft_filepicker_topk_003` registered in `common/src/constants.ts` and `scripts/ft-file-selection/relabel-for-offline-scoring.ts`. This model combines `ft_filepicker_topk_002`'s top-2 selection strategy with `ft_filepicker_010`'s message history blobbing. The offline scoring script now includes this model in the evaluation set, while `print-recent-relabels.ts` updates to display model and output details for better debugging. Backend `request-files-prompt.ts` logic simplified to always use `ft_filepicker_010` for production, removing experimental cost-mode branching.

eli5.text: The system now uses a single, improved method to guess which files are most relevant when you ask it a coding question, dropping an older experimental path that switched between two approaches. A new testing model was registered so engineers can compare how well it picks the top two files versus the single best file, and the offline scoring script now includes that test model in its comparisons. If you looked, you'd see the code no longer branches based on a cost setting-it always uses the established filepicker model-and the debug output for recent file selections now shows which model produced each result.

ai.title: Upgrade @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch to 0.12.0
ai.summary: Dependency `@homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch` upgraded from `0.12.0-beta.5` to stable `0.12.0` in `npm-app/package.json`. Replaces beta release with stable version. Scope limited to `npm-app` package definition.

eli5.text: The app swapped out a beta version of a helper tool that runs terminal-style commands behind the scenes for the final, ready-to-use version of the same helper. The assistant and its plug-in tools rely on this helper to talk to a system shell, and the new version should be more reliable and stable now that it is no longer a trial release. The change only affects the one part of the app that manages automation and plug-in integration, so most everyday use is unaffected, but it quietly makes the behind-the-scenes terminal work that powers some plug-in features slightly more dependable.

ai.title: Fix terminal ANSI parsing and hook commands
ai.summary: Split `stripColors` and `stripAnsi` in `common/src/util/string.ts` to handle OSC sequences correctly. Updated `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts` to use strict `IPty` types and dynamic needle patterns for command completion detection. `codebuff.json` hooks now separate unit tests from typechecking with simplified ANSI stripping.

eli5.text: The terminal window that runs commands now reads output correctly even when programs send special color and formatting codes, so prompts and results stop getting garbled or missed. When you run a command, the assistant can now tell for sure when the command is finished and reliably capture its full output. You would notice fewer cases where commands appear to hang, return empty results, or miss the final prompt.

ai.title: Extract waitForPreviousCheckpoint to sync tool execution
ai.summary: Refactor checkpoint synchronization logic into `waitForPreviousCheckpoint` in `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/checkpoint.ts`. `npm-app/src/client.ts` now awaits this helper before processing `str_replace`, `create_plan`, and `run_terminal_command` tool calls. Ensures previous file state saves complete before subsequent operations execute. Internal stability improvement for CLI checkpoint handling.

eli5.text: The assistant now waits for each saved checkpoint to fully finish before making its next file edit, terminal command, or plan, so you won't see a file save and a later edit step on to the same file happen at the same time and overwrite each other in this release. This behind-the-scenes fix lives inside the command-line version of the tool and only smooths out the order things happen in, with no buttons or settings to flip.

ai.title: Rename admin/organizations route to admin/orgs
ai.summary: Renamed `web/src/app/admin/organizations/page.tsx` to `web/src/app/admin/orgs/page.tsx` and updated internal API fetch paths from `/api/admin/organizations` to `/api/admin/orgs` and `/api/admin/organizations/export` to `/api/admin/orgs/export`. This standardizes URL slugs for the admin organization subsystem. The invite acceptance flow in `web/src/app/invites/[token]/page.tsx` now redirects to `/orgs/{slug}` instead of `/organizations/{slug}`.

eli5.text: When you accept an invitation to join an organization, you are now taken to a web address that uses 'orgs' instead of 'organizations' in the URL after you log in. The internal admin pages for managing organizations were also moved to a matching shorter address so the naming is consistent throughout the system. This is live now for anyone using the invitation link or the admin organization management pages.

ai.title: Add endturn to TOOLSWHICHENDTHERESPONSE
ai.summary: Added 'end_turn' to the TOOLS_WHICH_END_THE_RESPONSE array in backend/src/tools.ts. This ensures the agent correctly identifies end_turn as a stop sequence, terminating the response cycle appropriately. Scope limited to backend tool definitions.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes its turn, it can now use a specific instruction to signal that it's done responding, rather than relying on indirect cues. This was added to an internal list that defines which actions should cause the assistant to stop generating output and wait for the next message. If you interact with the assistant, you won't notice anything different, since this mainly helps the system manage its conversation flow more cleanly. The change is live as of today and only affects how the assistant handles response endings behind the scenes.

ai.title: Prompt tweaks: end turn after 1 fix attempt, ask mode flag copy
ai.summary: System prompt instructs agent to stop and call end_turn after one fix attempt, replacing previous multi-refinement guidance. Lite mode prompt branch removed; unified instruction now allows clarify-or-complete. CLI --ask flag description shortened to "won't change code" in npm-app/src/cli-definitions.ts. Unused isGPT4_1 constant deleted from backend/src/main-prompt.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant a question in the special Q&A mode, it will now answer once and stop, instead of going back and forth trying to fix things. This change is live today and affects only the Q&A mode, regular coding sessions still work the same way. The assistant's instructions were cleaned up to remove unused options, making it behave more predictably when answering questions.

ai.title: Refactor typecheck scripts to include dependencies
ai.summary: Removed `typecheck-only` script across packages. `typecheck` now runs `build` (which implies `typecheck-this-package`) to ensure dependencies are checked. Updated `codebuff.json` and CI workflows to use `bun run typecheck` instead of `bun run typecheck-only`.

eli5.text: The project's type-checking process was streamlined by removing a redundant step that only checked one package at a time. Previously, running type checks would validate only the current package without ensuring its dependencies were also valid. Now, type checking automatically builds and verifies all dependent packages first, catching errors that span multiple parts of the codebase. This change is live today and affects developers contributing to the project, making type errors easier to catch early.

ai.title: Allow createplan in ask mode
ai.summary: create_plan tool now permitted in ask mode via backend/src/tools.ts and main-prompt.ts. Previous logic excluded it alongside write_file and str_replace. Updated instructions allow overwriting plans with same filename, noting multiple uses are valid in ask mode.

eli5.text: When the assistant is in ask mode (answering questions rather than taking actions), it can now create a step-by-step plan the same way it can write a document or edit text. Previously, this planning feature was blocked in ask mode and treated the same as tools that modify files. Now, the assistant is also permitted to overwrite an existing plan by using the exact same file name, which means creating a plan with a name that already exists will replace the old one instead of being rejected.

ai.title: Reinforce ask mode tool restrictions
ai.summary: Added explicit system message instructing agent to avoid write_file and run_terminal_command when isAskMode is true. Prevents tool execution attempts in read-only ask mode. Scope: backend/src/main-prompt.ts. The message uses timeToLive 'agentStep' and asSystemMessage wrapper.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant questions instead of telling it to get work done, it will no longer try to use the tools that save or run things, because those tools have been turned off in that mode and attempting them would now produce a clear message rather than a failed attempt. This affects anyone using the assistant in the question-answering mode and they would notice the assistant simply refuses to write files or run commands when asked. The change is in place as of 2025-06-06.

ai.title: Enforce extreme conciseness in system prompts
ai.summary: Updated main-prompt.ts and agent-instructions.md to mandate extreme conciseness. Added explicit instruction to respond with minimal words (e.g., "4" instead of "2+2 equals 4"). Revised Buffy persona to prioritize brevity, removing filler phrases and requiring single-sentence answers where possible. Scope limited to backend system prompt configuration.

eli5.text: The assistant, known to developers as Buffy, was taught to speak in much shorter replies from now on, favoring brief answers over full sentences or explanations. A developer using the assistant daily would notice responses that cut straight to the point, with fewer friendly phrases and less detail, even when the answer could be expanded. This change is live today and only affects how the assistant formats its replies internally.

ai.title: Update createplan tool test snapshot
ai.summary: Snapshot for `create_plan` tool updated. Instructions revised to allow plan overwriting via same filename and permit repeated use in ask mode. Internal test fixture change.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to make a plan and save it to a file, you can now tell it to write a new plan to that same file name and it will simply replace the old plan instead of complaining that the file already exists. This only affects the internal instructions for how the assistant writes plans, so regular users won't notice anything different; it just makes the planning tool work like a regular document you can overwrite with a newer version when you need to revise your plan.

eli5.text: Nothing changed for you to see or use today. The software's internal version label was bumped from one number to the next, which is just a behind-the-scenes bookkeeping step that keeps automated tool tracking up to date. This particular update contains no new features, fixes, or behavior changes that you would notice. It is the kind of routine maintenance that happens between releases with actual user-facing improvements.

ai.title: Refactor auth utilities into shared @codebuff/internal package
ai.summary: Extracted authentication logic from backend and web into new `@codebuff/internal` package. Consolidated admin email lists and token validation into `packages/internal/src/utils/auth.ts`. Updated `backend`, `web`, and `evals` to depend on `@codebuff/internal` instead of duplicating auth code or using `@codebuff/integrations`.

eli5.text: The code that checks who is allowed to use the backend and who can log in to the admin panel used to live in two separate copies - one in the backend code and one in the web code. Both copies contained the same list of admin email addresses and the same logic for validating login tokens, so when the team needed to update either one, they had to remember to change it in two places. The team moved that duplicated authentication logic into a single shared location inside the codebase, and then pointed the backend, the website, and the evaluation tools at the new shared location so every part of the system now reads from the same source of truth. The list of admin email addresses was also carried over unchanged, so the same people who could previously access admin features can still do so.

ai.title: Add nx test targets to backend common npm-app
ai.summary: New `test` targets added to `backend/project.json`, `common/project.json`, and `npm-app/project.json` using `nx:run-commands` executor. Root `package.json` gains a `test` script running `nx run-many` across these three projects with `--skip-nx-cache`. Backend and Common are new project definitions; npm-app updates existing config. Commands execute `bun test` against `*.test.ts` files in each source root.

eli5.text: You can now type a single command, "npm test," and your project will automatically check its backend, shared code, and web application for broken pieces, all at once, instead of running each check separately. This combines the scattered testing steps into one organized routine, making it harder to skip tests before sharing your work. The project now understands how its pieces depend on each other so it can decide what needs checking when something changes.

ai.title: Custom file picker config for orgs
ai.summary: Added `custom-file-picker` feature flag support for organizations. New `org_feature` table stores JSON config for model selection and file limits. `getCustomFilePickerConfigForOrg` retrieves and validates config against `CustomFilePickerConfigSchema`. Falls back to defaults if config is missing, inactive, or invalid.

eli5.text: Organizations on the paid plan can now choose which file-selection model their team uses and set custom limits on how many files the assistant can look at at once. You’ll spot it when you open the file picker for your org: instead of the default behavior, you’ll see the model and file limits you chose. The company added a new settings page (stored in a database table) that lets org admins pick from the available models and adjust how many files to pull in for different tasks. If an org hasn’ set any preferences yet, or if the settings get removed, the file picker quietly reverts to the standard default behavior, so nothing breaks.
